synthesis.description: Schedulers and traders announce absences and name who covers for them, circulate weekend and holiday on-call schedules with cell and pager numbers, and send on-call notes after each weekend describing calls received and actions taken, such as gas control pages, meter problems reported by producers, and corrected confirms. Managers also arrange skeleton staff for holiday trading days and cover for affiliates.
steps: Someone announces an absence or a weekend or holiday that needs coverage.
A backup or on-call person is named, with contact numbers for the period.
The on-call schedule or contact sheet is updated and circulated.
The on-call person handles calls from gas control, pipelines and counterparties.
Actions taken are logged, including changed nominations or confirms.
On-call notes are sent to the team after the shift for follow-up.
synthesis.approach: Keep one shared on-call calendar and contact sheet that each person updates when they will be out, with backups named per pipeline or desk, and use a fixed on-call notes form that captures each call, the counterparty, the meter or contract, and the action taken.
synthesis.rationale: Coverage notices and weekend notes are free-form and scattered; a standard notes form and a single contact sheet make handovers complete, keep numbers current and show who covers what.
